name: MonarchTabularNumberStyle
title: TabularNumber
summary: Fixed-width digits for text, so that columns of figures line up and changing values do not jitter: a text style, and MonarchTabularNumber, which formats a number in the user's locale or shows a dash when there is none.
whenToUse: For figures in tables and lists, totals, counters and timers. Use MonarchTabularNumber(value) for a number that may be missing, MonarchTabularNumber(text) for text that is already formatted, and MonarchTabularNumberStyle.applyTo or spanStyle inside other text.
whenNotToUse: For money with its currency use a currency NumberFormat as format, or the app's money formatting; for a number inside a sentence that is not compared with others, plain MonarchText is enough.
api: object MonarchTabularNumberStyle { const val FONT_FEATURE_SETTINGS: String = "tnum"; fun applyTo(style: TextStyle): TextStyle; fun spanStyle(): SpanStyle }

@Composable fun MonarchTabularNumber(value: Number?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, style: MonarchTextStyle = MonarchTextStyle.Body, format: NumberFormat? = null, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, textAlign: TextAlign? = null, emptyText: String? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null)
@Composable fun MonarchTabularNumber(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, style: MonarchTextStyle = MonarchTextStyle.Body, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, textAlign: TextAlign? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The number, or null when there is none. A Double or Float that is NaN or infinite counts as missing.

options.name: text
options.description: In the second overload, text that is already formatted.

options.name: format
options.description: How the number is written: a number, percent or currency instance with its options. null is NumberFormat.getNumberInstance in the locale of the current configuration.

options.name: color
options.description: Unspecified uses the content color of the surrounding surface.

options.name: textAlign
options.description: Align columns of figures to the end.

options.name: emptyText
options.description: Shown in place of a missing number. Built in: an em dash (monarch_tabularnumber_empty).

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Read by TalkBack in place of a missing number. Built in: "No value" (monarch_tabularnumber_empty_label).

states.name: value
states.description: The formatted number in fixed-width digits.

states.name: missing
states.description: The value is null, NaN or infinite: an em dash is shown and TalkBack reads "No value".

appearance: The type role and color of the surrounding text; only the digits change to fixed width. Follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes like any MonarchText.
platformNotes: The web TabularNumber formats with Intl.NumberFormat; Android takes a java.text.NumberFormat, so every option of the platform (percent, currency, fraction digits, grouping) is available and nothing is re-implemented. The parity map named MonarchTypography; it has no tabular style, so Monarch ships MonarchTabularNumberStyle (the iOS name) and the MonarchTabularNumber composable in the same folder. The web never breaks a line inside a number; on Android a number that does not fit wraps, and maxLines is the app's choice through a plain Text with applyTo.
accessibility: A formatted number is read by TalkBack as its text.
A missing value is read as "No value" (or emptyLabel), not as a dash.
The text is in a type role in sp and grows with the font size setting.
Number formatting follows the locale of the configuration, including digits, grouping and decimal separators.
edgeCases: NaN and infinity are shown as missing, like null.
Only digits get one width. Separators, signs and currency symbols keep their own widths, so align columns to the end.
A custom font family without tabular digits is not changed by the style.
applyTo replaces other font feature settings of the style, because Compose holds them in one string.
A NumberFormat is mutable and not thread-safe; create it once with remember and do not share it across threads.
